themes_detail.label: Encampment Crisis Surge
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints spiked to 8 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 1.0 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 700% increase (z-score: 4.22)—signaling a sudden concentration of homelessness or street living in Washington Heights/Inwood that demands immediate investigation into causes and city response.
evidence: 8 encampment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike, z-score: 4.22)
Concurrent spike in urinating in public (3 complaints last week vs. 0.1 avg, 2300% increase)
Community board has repeatedly requested enhanced park safety and security staff, indicating long-standing resource gap
reporting_angles: Map encampment locations this week; interview outreach workers, Parks Enforcement, and neighbors about what triggered the sudden surge
Investigate whether this reflects a broader citywide trend or a district-specific push or resource gap; connect to CB's unfunded park safety requests

themes_detail.label: Dead/Dying Tree Spike
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints jumped to 3 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 0.2 per week (1100% spike, z-score: 6.35), suggesting accelerated tree decline or disease in public spaces that could affect air quality, canopy cover, and neighborhood character.
evidence: 3 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1100% spike, z-score: 6.35)
Community board has repeatedly requested park reconstruction and upgrades, suggesting broader maintenance backlog
383 building alteration permits filed in past 90 days; potential construction damage or tree stress from development
reporting_angles: Visit reported tree locations; interview Parks Department on disease or pest pressure in the district
Investigate whether construction permits and site activity correlate with tree decline; assess canopy loss trends

themes_detail.label: Street Public Urination Outbreak
themes_detail.summary: Urinating in public complaints spiked to 3 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 0.1 per week (2300% increase, z-score: 8.69)—tied to the concurrent encampment surge—indicating a sanitation and public health crisis in parks, streets, or transit areas.
evidence: 3 urinating in public complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69)
Coincides with 8 encampment complaints THIS WEEK (700% spike), suggesting homelessness and public health are linked
Community board requesting more frequent litter basket collection and park safety staff—unfunded requests indicate resource shortage
reporting_angles: Interview residents and business owners in affected areas about hygiene and safety concerns; identify geographic hotspots
Examine NYPD/Parks enforcement response; ask why park safety requests go unfunded while complaints accelerate

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Crackdown
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints jumped to 10 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 1.6 per week (515% increase, z-score: 5.06), suggesting either heightened regulatory action against street vendors or a spike in illegal vending that warrants scrutiny of enforcement priorities and vendor economics.
evidence: 10 vendor enforcement complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (515% spike, z-score: 5.06)
No clear community board complaints on vendor issues, suggesting this may be Department of Consumer Affairs action rather than resident concern
Concurrent with smoking/vaping spike (11 complaints last week, 167% increase), indicating broader street-level regulation activity
reporting_angles: Interview street vendors and community organizations; determine whether enforcement is targeting illegal vending or legal operators disproportionately
Contact DCCS and NYPD to understand enforcement surge—is this coordinated policy or reactive to complaints?

themes_detail.label: Smoking/Vaping Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Smoking or vaping complaints rose to 11 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 4.1 per week (167% increase, z-score: 4.26), indicating emerging resident frustration with secondhand smoke, vaping, or enforcement gaps in parks, residential, or transit areas.
evidence: 11 smoking/vaping complaints LAST WEEK vs. 4.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (167% spike, z-score: 4.26)
Concurrent with vendor enforcement spike, suggesting broader street-behavior regulation focus
No specific community board requests targeting smoking enforcement, suggesting this is grassroots resident concern rather than organized advocacy
reporting_angles: Interview complainants about where smoking/vaping is occurring and why enforcement has felt insufficient
Check whether city health or Parks enforcement has new directives or resources; compare to citywide enforcement trends
